question: Explain the difference between Vue 2 Options API and Vue 3 Composition API (<script setup>).
idealAnswer: Options API organizes code by component options (data, methods, computed, mounted). Composition API organizes code by logical feature concern using reactive primitives (ref, reactive) inside <script setup>, improving TypeScript support and composable logic reuse.
ideal_answer: Options API organizes code by component options (data, methods, computed, mounted). Composition API organizes code by logical feature concern using reactive primitives (ref, reactive) inside <script setup>, improving TypeScript support and composable logic reuse.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Architecture and Options API vs Composition API comprehension.

question: How does Vue 3 Reactivity work internally using ES6 Proxy vs Vue 2 Object.defineProperty()?
idealAnswer: Vue 2 used Object.defineProperty to intercept getters/setters, unable to detect new property additions or array index mutations. Vue 3 uses ES6 Proxies to intercept all object operations, tracking dependencies during read (track) and triggering re-renders on mutation (trigger).
ideal_answer: Vue 2 used Object.defineProperty to intercept getters/setters, unable to detect new property additions or array index mutations. Vue 3 uses ES6 Proxies to intercept all object operations, tracking dependencies during read (track) and triggering re-renders on mutation (trigger).
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Reactivity and Vue 3 Proxy Reactivity System comprehension.

question: What is the difference between 'ref()' and 'reactive()' in Vue 3, and when should you use each?
idealAnswer: 'ref()' wraps any value (primitives or objects) in a Ref object accessed via .value (automatically unwrapped in templates). 'reactive()' creates a deep reactive proxy exclusively for objects/arrays and loses reactivity if destructured without toRefs().
ideal_answer: 'ref()' wraps any value (primitives or objects) in a Ref object accessed via .value (automatically unwrapped in templates). 'reactive()' creates a deep reactive proxy exclusively for objects/arrays and loses reactivity if destructured without toRefs().
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Reactivity and ref vs reactive comprehension.

question: Explain Computed Properties in Vue and how they differ from standard Methods regarding caching.
idealAnswer: Computed properties are lazily evaluated and cached based on their reactive dependencies, re-evaluating only when dependencies change. Methods execute on every render regardless of whether dependencies changed.
ideal_answer: Computed properties are lazily evaluated and cached based on their reactive dependencies, re-evaluating only when dependencies change. Methods execute on every render regardless of whether dependencies changed.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Core Concepts and Computed vs Methods comprehension.

question: What is the difference between 'watch' and 'watchEffect' in Vue 3 Composition API?
idealAnswer: 'watch' explicitly tracks specified reactive sources and provides old and new values lazily. 'watchEffect' runs immediately and automatically tracks all reactive dependencies accessed inside its callback.
ideal_answer: 'watch' explicitly tracks specified reactive sources and provides old and new values lazily. 'watchEffect' runs immediately and automatically tracks all reactive dependencies accessed inside its callback.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Reactivity and watch vs watchEffect comprehension.

question: Explain Vue Single File Components (.vue): <template>, <script>, and <style scoped>.
idealAnswer: SFCs encapsulate HTML template, JavaScript logic, and CSS in a single .vue file. '<style scoped>' adds a unique data attribute (data-v-hash) to HTML elements and CSS selectors, preventing style leakage.
ideal_answer: SFCs encapsulate HTML template, JavaScript logic, and CSS in a single .vue file. '<style scoped>' adds a unique data attribute (data-v-hash) to HTML elements and CSS selectors, preventing style leakage.

question: What is v-model in Vue 3, and how do you implement two-way data binding with multiple v-models on custom components?
idealAnswer: v-model is syntactic sugar for passing a prop ('modelValue') and listening for an update event ('update:modelValue'). Vue 3 supports multiple v-models on a single component (v-model:first, v-model:last) and defineModel() macro in Vue 3.4+.
ideal_answer: v-model is syntactic sugar for passing a prop ('modelValue') and listening for an update event ('update:modelValue'). Vue 3 supports multiple v-models on a single component (v-model:first, v-model:last) and defineModel() macro in Vue 3.4+.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Components and v-model & Custom Component Binding comprehension.

question: Explain Component Communication in Vue: Props, Emits, Provide/Inject, and Event Bus.
idealAnswer: Parent-to-child communication uses props; child-to-parent uses emits (defineEmits). For deeply nested component hierarchies, provide/inject passes dependencies without prop drilling across intermediate layers.
ideal_answer: Parent-to-child communication uses props; child-to-parent uses emits (defineEmits). For deeply nested component hierarchies, provide/inject passes dependencies without prop drilling across intermediate layers.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Component Communication and Props, Emits, and Provide/Inject comprehension.

question: Explain Vue 3 Lifecycle Hooks (onMounted, onUpdated, onUnmounted) and how they map to Vue 2 options.
idealAnswer: Vue 3 Composition API provides lifecycle hooks: onMounted runs after initial DOM render; onUpdated runs after reactive state changes re-render the DOM; onUnmounted runs during component teardown to clean up timers/listeners.
ideal_answer: Vue 3 Composition API provides lifecycle hooks: onMounted runs after initial DOM render; onUpdated runs after reactive state changes re-render the DOM; onUnmounted runs during component teardown to clean up timers/listeners.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Lifecycle and Vue 3 Lifecycle Hooks comprehension.

question: What are Custom Composables in Vue 3, and how do they replace Vue 2 Mixins without naming collisions?
idealAnswer: Composables are functions that encapsulate and share stateful logic using Vue's Composition API (e.g. useMousePosition()). Unlike Mixins, composables make dependencies explicit, allow destructuring with renaming, and prevent property collision conflicts.
ideal_answer: Composables are functions that encapsulate and share stateful logic using Vue's Composition API (e.g. useMousePosition()). Unlike Mixins, composables make dependencies explicit, allow destructuring with renaming, and prevent property collision conflicts.

question: Explain Slots in Vue: Default Slots, Named Slots, and Scoped Slots with slot-scope/v-slot.
idealAnswer: Slots allow parent components to inject custom HTML/components into child layout placeholders (<slot>). Named slots (<slot name='header'>) target specific sections; Scoped slots (<slot :item='item'>) pass data from child back to parent template slot.
ideal_answer: Slots allow parent components to inject custom HTML/components into child layout placeholders (<slot>). Named slots (<slot name='header'>) target specific sections; Scoped slots (<slot :item='item'>) pass data from child back to parent template slot.

question: What is Pinia in Vue 3, and why has it replaced Vuex as the official state management library?
idealAnswer: Pinia is the official Vue state store. It eliminates Vuex mutations (allowing direct state modification in actions), offers first-class TypeScript inference, has no nested module complexity, and supports lightweight modular stores.
ideal_answer: Pinia is the official Vue state store. It eliminates Vuex mutations (allowing direct state modification in actions), offers first-class TypeScript inference, has no nested module complexity, and supports lightweight modular stores.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js State Management and Pinia vs Vuex comprehension.

question: Explain Vue Router: Route Navigation Guards (beforeEach, beforeRouteEnter) and Dynamic Route Matching.
idealAnswer: Vue Router manages single-page client routing. Navigation guards (router.beforeEach) intercept route transitions to perform authentication checks, permission validation, or cancel transitions before components render.

question: What are Teleport and Suspense built-in components in Vue 3?
idealAnswer: <Teleport to='body'> renders a component's template into a different DOM node outside its parent hierarchy (ideal for modals/tooltips). <Suspense> coordinates async component loading and displays fallback templates while waiting.
ideal_answer: <Teleport to='body'> renders a component's template into a different DOM node outside its parent hierarchy (ideal for modals/tooltips). <Suspense> coordinates async component loading and displays fallback templates while waiting.

question: How does Virtual DOM diffing work in Vue 3, and what compiler optimizations (Patch Flags, Hoisting, Block Tree) make it fast?
idealAnswer: Vue 3 compiler analyzes templates statically at build time: Static Hoisting moves unchanging VNodes outside render functions; Patch Flags tag dynamic nodes with bitmasks (text, class, style), allowing the diff algorithm to skip static nodes entirely.
ideal_answer: Vue 3 compiler analyzes templates statically at build time: Static Hoisting moves unchanging VNodes outside render functions; Patch Flags tag dynamic nodes with bitmasks (text, class, style), allowing the diff algorithm to skip static nodes entirely.
explanation: Evaluates Vue.js Internals & Performance and Vue 3 Compiler Optimizations comprehension.
